# Verification and Test-Coverage Requirements Quality Checklist: Identity and Foundation

**Purpose**: Validate that the slice's verification requirements — the Test Coverage Request, the success criteria's measurement rules, the exception closures, and the evidence obligations — are complete, unambiguous, consistent, and measurable before implementation begins.
**Created**: 2026-11-02
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) — 55 functional requirements, 62 acceptance criteria, 9 success criteria

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness — The Test Coverage Request and Its Gate

- [x] CHK001 Are the three test classes the request names — unit, integration, and end-to-end — each given their own object of coverage and their own boundary, with every requested behaviour assigned to exactly one class, so a rule is not requested twice with two expected outcomes? [Completeness, Consistency, Spec §Test Coverage Request; Constitution III]
- [x] CHK002 Is the request bound to the acceptance criteria by a stated rule — each of the 62 criteria exercised by at least one requested test, written before implementation and failing first — or does the artifact set require only that each criterion be referenced by a task, which an implementation task can satisfy with no test? [Gap, Traceability, Spec §Test Coverage Request, §Acceptance Criteria; Constitution Artifact Workflow]
- [x] CHK003 Is the 80% target's measurement stated completely — the changed-line denominator, the diff baseline it is taken against, and the constitution's exemption of generated code, migrations, and snapshots — so the gate cannot be met by a favourable count and does not read as applying to lines the constitution exempts? [Clarity, Measurability, Spec §Test Coverage Request (Coverage target); Constitution III]
- [x] CHK004 Is the coverage exclusion a closed list tied to `EX-007`, so a runtime behaviour absent from the list cannot be excluded from the target without a new exception row, and a behaviour on the list cannot lose its exception silently? [Completeness, Consistency, Spec §Test Coverage Request (Coverage target); Exception register `EX-007`]
- [x] CHK005 Is the point at which the coverage gate blocks named — the checkpoint (P1, per story, or R1 acceptance) and the artifact that reports it — so the threshold has an enforcement moment and not only a measurement? [Measurability, Gap, Spec §Test Coverage Request (Coverage target); Plan §Implementation Sequencing B8]

## Scenario and Edge-Case Coverage — Journeys, Concurrency, Time

- [x] CHK025 Are the concurrency cases — two sign-ups for one number, two entries of one code, a change and a reset submitted together — given a determinism rule for how simultaneity is produced and how many interleavings are exercised, so "arrive together" is testable rather than probabilistic? - [x] CHK027 Is every failure path of the messaging channel — a refusal at acceptance and a request timeout — asserted at both placements, the fresh request and the re-request, as FR-034 distinguishes them? [Coverage, Completeness, Spec §FR-034, §Test Coverage Request (Integration tests); Plan §Verification Notes (Enumeration uniformity)]
- [x] CHK028 Are the journeys the request withholds from end-to-end — US2's sign-out and sign-out of every device, US4, and US6 — each mapped to a named unit or integration test, or left as "the unit and integration tests named above"? [Coverage, Traceability, Spec §Test Coverage Request (End-to-end tests)]
- [x] CHK029 Are the removed-account and blocked-account states, reached directly because this slice ships no act that produces them, stated as an accepted substitute together with what the substitution cannot prove? [Assumption, Coverage, Spec §Test Coverage Request (Integration tests), §US4; Plan §Complexity Tracking row 18]
- [x] CHK030 Are the negative and temporal invariants — no email address, no session cap, no account before verification, and the row-level creation rule at every point the sign-up flow passes — each given a failing case as well as a passing assertion, so a test cannot pass on the happy path alone or on one observation? ### Review 2026-11-04 (CHK002, CHK005)

**Review line**: reviewed 2026-11-04 against `tasks.md` after the operational-state
pass — CHK002 and CHK005 are satisfied; the file still reads 38 marked, 0 open
(38/38), and no marker changed.

- **CHK002 — closed.** Every one of the 62 acceptance criteria is exercised by at
  least one requested test task, AC-059–AC-062 included: T149 exercises AC-059,
  T150 exercises AC-060, T152 exercises AC-061, and T151 exercises AC-062. The
  four operational criteria are cross-cutting, and their tests sit in the final
  phase where the assembled service is exercised; each fails when the rule it

  first response was lost, T148 for the service's and the store's unavailability
  and the provider's outage, T145 and T154 for the record's schema, order, and
  provisioning failure, and T153 for the operational rows' bound.
- **CHK005 — closed.** T155 names the point at which the coverage gate blocks —
  R1's acceptance, not the P1 checkpoint — and the artifact that reports it: the
  changed-line report attached to the pull request and kept in the `r1-acceptance`
  release, naming the diff baseline, the changed-line count, the covered count,
  the percentage, and every excluded path with its exception row. `README.md`
  records that R1's acceptance MUST NOT be recorded while the gate fails, so the
  threshold has an enforcement moment and a report rather than only a measurement.
